NOTICE
Notice is hereby given that the Twenty Seventh (27th) Annual General Meeting (“the AGM / 27th AGM”) of the Members of IRB 
Infrastructure Developers Limited (“the Company”) will be held on Thursday, September 18, 2025, at 03:00 pm (IST) through 
Video Conferencing (“VC”) / Other Audio Visual Means (“OAVM”) to transact the following business:
ORDINARY BUSINESS
1.  To consider and adopt the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, together 
with the Report of the Auditors thereon.
2.  To consider and adopt the Audited Standalone Financial Statements for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, together 
with the Reports of the Board of Directors and the Auditors thereon.
3.  To appoint a Director in place of Mrs. Deepali V. Mhaiskar (DIN: 00309884), Whole-time Director who retires by rotation 
and, being eligible, seeks re-appointment.
SPECIAL BUSINESS
4.  To consider and, if thought fit, to pass with or without modification(s), the following resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
  “RESOLVED THAT  pursuant to the provisions of Section 148(3) and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies 
Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 (including any statutory modification(s) or re-
enactment(s) thereof, for the time being in force), the remuneration payable to M/s. Joshi Apte & Associates, Practicing 
Cost Accountant having Firm Registration No. 00240 appointed by the Board of Directors of the Company to conduct the 
audit of the cost records of the Company for the financial year 2025-26, amounting to `3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakh 
only) p.a. plus applicable taxes and reimbursement of out-of-pocket expenses at actuals, if any, incurred in connection 
with the audit, be and is hereby ratified and confirmed.
  RESOLVED FURTHER THAT  the Board of Directors or Key Managerial Personnel of the Company be and are hereby 
authorised to do all acts, deed and things, proper or desirable to give effect to this Resolution.”
5. To consider and, if thought fit, to pass with or without modification(s), the following resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
  “RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Section 204 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with the Companies 
(Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014 and Regulation 24A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof for the 
time being in force, M/s. Mihen Halani & Associates, Practising Company Secretary (Membership No. FCS 9926), be and is 
hereby appointed as the Secretarial Auditors of the Company, for a term of five consecutive financial years commencing 
from April 1, 2025 till March 31, 2030, at such remuneration plus applicable taxes and other out-of-pocket expenses and 
on such terms and conditions as may be determined by the Board of Directors of the Company in consultation with the 
Secretarial Auditors of the Company. 
  RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors or Key Managerial Personnel of the Company be and are hereby 
authorised to do all acts, deed and things, proper or desirable to give effect to this Resolution.”
By Order of the Board of Directors

Item No.4
The Board of Directors of the Company has appointed 
M/s. Joshi Apte & Associates, Practicing Cost Accountant, to 
conduct the audit of the cost records of the Company for the 
financial year 2025-26. In terms of the provisions of Section 
148(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 14(a)
(ii) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, the 
remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor is to be ratified by the 
Members of the Company. The remuneration of `3,00,000/- 
(Rupees Three lakh only) per annum is payable to M/s. Joshi 
Apte & Associates, Practicing Cost Accountant for the audit 
to be conducted for financial year 2025-26. Accordingly, the 
Members are requested to ratify the remuneration payable to 
the Cost Auditors for the audit to be conducted for financial 
year 2025-26.
None of the Directors, Key Managerial Personnel of the 
Company and their relatives, are in any way concerned or 
interested, financial or otherwise, in the said Resolution.
The Board of Directors recommends the Ordinary Resolution 
set out at Item No. 4 of the Notice for approval by the Members.
Item No.5
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 204 and other 
applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, read with 
Rule 9 of the Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of 
Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014, as amended from time to 
time, every listed company is required to annex a Secretarial 
Audit Report, issued by a Company Secretary in Practice, to 
its Board’s Report.
Additionally, in accordance with Regulation 24A of the 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, as amended, every listed entity is 
mandated to undertake a Secretarial Audit conducted 
by a Peer Reviewed Company Secretary in Practice. The 
appointment of such Secretarial Auditor must be approved 
by the members at the Annual General Meeting.
In view of the above regulatory requirements the appointment 
of such Secretarial Auditor must be approved for a tenure of 
five years by the members at the Annual General Meeting, 
accordingly after evaluating various parameters such as 
industry experience, audit team competence, efficiency, and 
independence, the Board of Directors of the Company, at its 
meeting held on August 14, 2025, approved the appointment 
of M/s. Mihen Halani & Associates, Practicing Company 
Secretaries (Membership No. FCS 9926), as the Secretarial 
Auditors of the Company for a term of five consecutive 
financial years commencing from FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-
30. The said appointment is subject to the approval of the 
members at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.The Secretarial Auditors shall be remunerated as mutually 
agreed upon by the Board of Directors and the Auditors, in 
addition to applicable taxes and reimbursement of out-of-
pocket expenses.
M/s. Mihen Halani & Associates, Practising Company 
Secretaries (‘MHA’) established in 2013 and based in 
Mumbai offers specialized corporate governance and 
company secretarial services. With skilled team experienced 
across diverse sectors, MHA supports in implementing 
effective governance frameworks for listed, unlisted, and 
multinational companies.
MHA has a dynamic and experienced team with deep 
expertise in company law, governance, and legal advisory 
across various sectors and industries. MHA is known for 
its adherence to the highest professional standards, timely 
service delivery, and strong ethical values. These principles 
have enabled the firm to support organizations in achieving 
robust governance practices and long-term value creation.
MHA has confirmed its eligibility to be appointed as 
Secretarial Auditors in terms of Regulation 24A of the Listing 
Regulations read with SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-
PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024. The 
firm has been Peer Reviewed by the Institute of Company 
Secretaries of India (ICSI), ensuring the highest standards in 
professional practices.
None of the Directors, Key Managerial Personnel of the 
Company and their relatives, are in any way concerned or 
interested, financial or otherwise, in the said Resolution.
The Board of Directors recommends the Ordinary Resolution 
set forth in Item No.5 of the Notice for approval by 
the Members.

NOTES
1.  The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (‘MCA’), vide its General 
Circular No. 20/2020 dated May 5, 2020 read with 
General Circular Nos. 14/2020 dated April 08, 2020, and 
subsequent circulars issued in this regard, the latest being 
09/2024 dated September 19, 2024 (‘MCA Circulars’), 
has allowed the Companies to conduct the Annual 
General Meeting (AGM) through Video Conferencing or 
Other Audio-Visual Means (‘VC/OAVM’) till September 30, 
2025. In compliance with the provisions of the Companies 
Act, 2013 (“Act”), SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”) 
and MCA Circulars, the AGM of the Company is being 
held through VC/OAVM.
2.  The Company has enabled the Members to participate 
at the AGM through the VC/OAVM facility provided by 
KFin Technologies Limited, Registrar and Share Transfer 
Agents (“KFintech / RTA”). The Members can join the 
AGM in the VC/OAVM mode 15 minutes before the 
scheduled time of the commencement of the Meeting. 
The instructions for participation by Members are given in 
the subsequent pages. Participation at the AGM through 
VC shall be allowed on a first-come-first-served basis for 
first 1,000 members. This will not include large Members 
(Members holding 2% or more equity shares), Promoters, 
Institutional Investors, Directors, Key Managerial 
Personnel, the Chairpersons of the Audit Committee, 
Stakeholders Relationship Committee, Auditors etc. who 
are allowed to attend the AGM without restriction on 
account of first-come-first-served basis. The members 
can visit https://emeetings.kfintech.com  and login 
through existing user id and password to attend the live 
proceedings of the AGM of the Company.
3.  Members may note that pursuant to the provisions of MCA 
and SEBI Circulars, the Annual report for the financial year 
2024-25 and AGM Notice (including remote e-voting 
instructions) is being sent to Members electronically. 
Accordingly, the Annual Report for the financial year 
2024-25 and AGM Notice are being sent only to those 
members whose names appear in the Register of 
Members / List of Beneficial Owners as on August 15, 
2025 received from the Depositories and whose e-mail 
addresses are registered with the Company or with the 
depository participant / depository. Members may note 
that the Annual Report for the financial year 2024-25 
and AGM Notice will also be available on the Company’s 
website at www.irb.co.in , websites of Stock Exchange(s) 
i.e. BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India 
Limited a t www.bseindia.com  and www.nseindia.com  
respectively and on the website of KFintech at https://
evoting.kfintech.com /.
4.  As per the Circulars mentioned above, the Members may 
also note that the Company would not be sending the 
Annual Report for the financial year 2024-25 and AGM notice by post to the members whose e-mail address is not 
registered with the Company or depository participants/
depository.
5.  The Company is providing a facility to the members 
as on the cut-off date, being Thursday, September 11, 
2025 (“the cut-off date”)  to exercise their right to vote 
on the matters listed in the Notice by electronic voting 
systems (Remote e-voting). Additionally, the members can 
also exercise their right to vote by e-voting during the 
AGM. The process and manner of remote e-voting with 
necessary User ID and password is given below. Such 
remote e-voting facility  is in addition to voting that will 
take place at the AGM being held through VC/OAVM. Any 
person who acquires shares of the company and becomes 
a member of the company after the dispatch of the Notice, 
and holding shares as on the cut-off date, may obtain the 
User ID and Password by sending a request at evoting@
kfintech.com  or contact KFintech at toll free number  
1-800-309-4001. Voting by electronic mode is a 
convenient means of exercising voting rights and may 
help to increase the member’s participation in the 
decision-making process.
6.  The Members who have cast their vote prior to the 
meeting by remote e-voting may also attend the AGM 
but shall not be entitled to vote again. Once a vote is 
cast by a member, he / she shall not be allowed to alter it 
subsequently. In case a Member casts his / her vote, both 
by Remote e-Voting and e-voting at the AGM mode, then 
the voting done by Remote e-Voting shall prevail and the 
e-voting at the AGM shall be invalid.
7.  Pursuant to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, a 
Member entitled to attend and vote at the AGM is entitled 
to appoint a proxy to attend and vote on his/her behalf and 
the proxy need not be a Member of the Company. Since 
this AGM is being held through VC, physical attendance 
of Members has been dispensed with. Accordingly, the 
facility for appointment of proxies by the Members will 
not be available for the AGM and hence the Proxy Form, 
Attendance Slip and Route Map are not annexed to 
this Notice.
8.  The members attending the meeting through VC/OAVM 
shall be counted for the purpose of reckoning the quorum 
of the meeting under Section 103 of the Act.
9.  The Company has appointed “M/s. Mihen Halani & 
Associates”, Practicing Company Secretaries, as the 
Scrutinizer to scrutinize the e-voting process in a fair 
and transparent manner. The Scrutinizer will submit his 
report after completion of the scrutiny to the Chairman 
and Managing Director of the Company or any person 
authorized by him. The result of the e-voting will be 
announced within 2 working days of conclusion of the 
AGM and the same will be communicated to the National 
Stock Exchange of India Limited and the BSE Limited 
and shall also be available on the Company’s website  
www.irb.co.in and on KFintech’s web link

17.  In terms of Regulation 40(1) of Listing Regulations, 
as amended from time to time, transfer, transmission 
and transposition of securities shall be effected only 
in dematerialized form. In view of this and to eliminate 
all risks associated with physical shares and for ease 
of portfolio management, members holding shares in 
physical form are requested to consider converting their 
holdings to dematerialized form.
  Members may please note that SEBI, vide its Master 
Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/POD-1/P/CIR/2024/37 
dated May 07, 2024 (earlier Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/
MIRSD_RTAMB/ P/CIR/2022/8 dated January 25, 2022), 
has mandated Listed Companies to issue securities 
in dematerialized form only while processing service 
requests viz. Issue of duplicate securities certificate; 
claim from Unclaimed Suspense Account; Renewal/
Exchange of securities certificate; Endorsement; Sub-
division/Splitting of securities certificate; Consolidation 
of securities certificates/folios; Transmission and 
Transposition. Accordingly, Members are requested to 
make service requests by submitting a duly filled and 
signed Form ISR–4, the format of which is available on 
the Company’s website under the weblink at https://www.
irb.co.in/home/information-to-physical-shareholders-2/  
and on the website of the Company’s RTA at https://ris.
kfintech.com . It may be noted that any service request can 
be processed only after the folio is KYC compliant.
  However SEBI vide its circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-
PoD/P/CIR/2025/97 dated July 02, 2025 has allowed to 
open a special window only for re-lodgement of transfer

In today’s ever-changing dynamic digital landscape, security, 
foolproof systems and efficiency in identity verification are 
paramount. We understand the need to protect the interests of 
you (members) and also comply with KYC standards. Ensuring 
security and KYC compliance is paramount of importance 
in today’s remote world. Digital identity verification, using 
biometrics and digital ID document checks, helps combat fraud, 
even when individuals aren’t physically present. To counteract 
common spoofing attempts, we engage in capturing liveness 
detection and facial comparison technology.
We are excited to announce that our RTA has introduced an 
Online Personal Verification (OPV) process, based on liveness 
detection and document verification.
Key Benefits:
•		A	fully	digital	process,	 only	requiring	 internet	access	and	
a device.
•		Effectively	 reduces	 fraud	for	remote	 and	unknown 	 
applicants.
•	 Supports	KYC	requirements.
Here’s how it works:
I. Users receive a link via e-mail and SMS.
II.  Users record a video, take a selfie, and capture an image 
with their PAN card.
III.  Facial comparison ensures the user’s identity matches 
their verified ID (PAN).Wha tsApp:

avail bouquet of services.

Infrastructure. 
Sustainable  Growth.
Sustainable infrastructure goes beyond 
green buildings, efficient transit systems, electric mobility, and renewable energy. It is about building resilient foundations  that enable communities, businesses, and ecosystems to thrive and flourish over the long term. It means envisioning growth with purpose, investing with foresight, executing with responsibility, and delivering value to all stakeholders, ensuring that the infrastructure built today meets current needs without compromising the needs of future generations. It entails developing infrastructure that is environmentally sustainable, economically viable, socially inclusive, and resilient to the growing challenges of climate change.
At IRB, India’s leading and largest multi-
national developer in the roads and highways sector, we are committed to developing safe, sustainable, and world-class infrastructure, thereby contributing to a developing nation in its Amrit Kaal.
Over the past year, we have taken 
significant strides to embed sustainability into every aspect of our strategy – from reducing carbon footprints and integrating renewable energy solutions to adopting smart technologies and promoting inclusive development. We aim to lead by example, fostering innovation that serves both people and the planet.We endeavour to imbibe a culture of sustainability across all levels of the organisation. Our approach  is rooted in environmental consciousness, operational excellence, social responsibility, and strong governance. Our goal is not only to achieve defined targets but to make sustainability an integral part of our day-to-day operations.  
We recognise that 
sustainable infrastructure is the cornerstone for sustainable growth,  fuelling economic activity, social development, and protecting the environment. We remain committed to building infrastructure that contributes meaningfully to a more equitable, resilient, and sustainable future for the nation.To download this report or to

About the Report
Basis of Reporting 
The Integrated Reporting <IR> principles have globally 
become a benchmark for best practice in corporate reporting for their transparency and disclosures beyond statutory norms. 
This is our first year of integrated reporting based on 
International Integrated Reporting Framework <IR> developed by the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC), now part of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Foundation. This reporting is in line with our philosophy of transparently disclosing information beyond the statutory norms. We have tried to provide insights into our value creation process and factors that may affect it. The Report covers the six capitals – financial, manufactured, human, intellectual, social & relationship and natural – that we use in our business. Further, we cover information on material matters, governance, performance and prospects in context of  
the external environment. 
Reporting Principle 
This Report has been prepared in accordance with:
•  Companies Act, 2013 (and the Rules made thereunder)
•  Indian Accounting Standards, the SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 
• Secretarial Standards
•  Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report  
(BRSR - under listing obligation)
Other international guidelines in accordance with:
•  <IR> framework of International Integrated Reporting 
Council (IIRC)
• Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards
• United Nations Global Compact (UNGC)
•  United Nations Sustainable Development Goals  
(UN SDGs)
Boundary and Scope of Reporting 
The Report covers both financial and non-financial information and activities on a consolidated basis for  IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd., including its subsidiary companies and their associates, for the period from April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025.
External Assurance

NATURAL CAPIT AL

IRB at a Glance
India’s leading and the largest roads and 
highways infrastructure developer
IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd. (IRB) is India’s first Integrated Multi-National Transport 
Infrastructure Developer in Roads & Highways segment, with a marquee portfolio that includes landmark projects like the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, Ahmedabad-Vadodara Expressway, and Hyderabad Outer Ring Road.
Our Ethos
The purpose for our existence 
is to express and demonstrate our sincere and whole hearted commitment towards our Society and the Nation, through the creation of World Class Roads & Highways Infrastructure, with minimum impact to the nature and recycling of product to maximum extent, which will facilitate creation of a strong sense of belongingness among people and bring them closer through quicker connectivity that we establish to boost trade and businesses, entrepreneurships, job opportunities; socio-cultural developments to help economy grow and enhance stakeholders’ value through profitability and goodwill.To create the comprehensive network of world class roads and highways infrastructure in India that will bring cities and citizens closer, share and exchange values to ensure socio-economic and cultural development of the Nation.
To strengthen and grow to the 
leadership position by ensuring continual improvements in operational efficiencies, quality and services.To become India’s largest, most admired, trustworthy, respected and stakeholders friendly organization, committed to develop safe and comfortable roads and highways infrastructure for the Nation.
PURPOSE MISSION India First
Each and every one of us at IRB strives to fulfill developmental aspirations of the Nation.
Quality, Reliability & Safety
We make sure that our infrastructure projects are of the supreme quality, highly reliable and safe for users.
Morality & Ethics
Our conduct and actions will at all times be moral and ethical. We would never resort to any action or work or involve in such an acts, which are illegal, immoral and/or unethical.
Ownership & Stability
Each one of us at IRB is committed to function with high responsibility, like a stakeholder, so as to ensure growth, stability and sense of security for the organization.
Trust & Integrity
Our rich domain expertise and high project execution skills; cost effectiveness and profitability; fair and transparent business practices constitute the bedrock of our policy for creating high level of trust and integrity about us among the stakeholders.
Openness and Transparency for  
Organizational Growth
We promote work environment that gives equal 
opportunity to each and every employee to develop and grow within the organization. We embrace and encourage the culture of openness to dialogue, free-fair-frank-firm- and fearless expression of views and opinions for creating a robust and adapted organization for meeting challenges in the fast changing business environment.VALUES

Chairman and MD’s Message
Dear Stakeholders,
If I were to 
describe Financial Year 2024-25 for IRB in one word, it would be - “Year of Resilience”.
FY 2024-25 was not without 
its share of headwinds, but it was precisely during these moments that the strength of our platform, the clarity of our strategy, and the commitment of our people came to the fore.FY 2024-25 was a challenging year – both globally and for 
India. The global environment remained uncertain, impacted by persistent geopolitical tensions, volatile commodity prices, and disruptions in international trade. Domestically, the year commenced with the General Elections, which led to a temporary slowdown in economic activity. Decision-making across government bodies and public institutions was understandably cautious during this period, resulting in subdued momentum in infrastructure project awards and delays in policy rollouts. In addition, traffic volumes across key corridors remained muted in the first half, reflecting the broader softness in economic growth. 
FY 2024-25 was not without its share of headwinds, but it 
was precisely during these moments that the strength of our platform, the clarity of our strategy, and the commitment of our people came to the fore. We navigated this environment with agility, took prudent decisions, and remained focused on our long-term value creation roadmap.
Despite these challenges, we have demonstrated 
remarkable resilience. In a year marked by shifting market sentiments, evolving regulatory landscapes, and macroeconomic uncertainty, we stood firm – delivering tangible progress, sustaining operational momentum, and reinforcing stakeholder confidence. The second half of the year saw a strong recovery in both traffic volumes and project activity, reaffirming the robustness of our business model and execution capabilities. We added two TOT assets to our portfolio during the year, with operations commencing at the start of FY 2024-25. Both assets have delivered performance well ahead of initial expectations – driven by robust traffic volumes and a seamless operational ramp-up. This early outperformance underscores the effectiveness of our asset selection and due diligence framework, while reinforcing our conviction in the long-term value creation potential of the TOT model.
We also recorded a 23% Y-o-Y increase in toll revenues 
across IRB and the Private InvIT portfolio – nearly twice the national average growth of 12.5% . This strong 
performance underscores the strategic positioning, 
operational excellence, and inherent resilience  of our 
asset base, but also the impact of timely asset additions –  reaffirming the strength and stability of our platform across economic cycles.
The Private InvIT continues to be strongly cash-flow 
accretive , having declared cumulative distributions of approximately ` 2,438 Mn in FY 2024-25. With a 51% 
holding, IRB has been a direct beneficiary of these steady payouts, contributing meaningfully  to our liquidity 
position  and further reinforcing the InvIT platform’s role as 
a reliable and recurring source of cash flows .
The ` 800 Bn+ asset base we have built over the years 
is now reaping the benefits of scale and quality – generating stable and growing cash flows across platforms. It stands as a testament to the foresight, discipline, and long-term vision that have shaped IRB’s journey over the last two decades.
As we reflect on the year gone by, it is evident that IRB’s 
journey is defined not just by growth, but by the quality and consistency of that growth – grounded in strong, governance, strategic foresight, and an unwavering commitment to nation-building.
Implementation of the B.E.S.T. Policy
As discussed previously, we had outlined our B.E.S.T. strategy – Bid, Execute, Stabilise and Transfer.  I am 
pleased to share that we have reinvigorated this policy in FY 2024-25 .
We have initiated the process of transferring three mature BOT assets  from IRB Infrastructure Trust to the IRB InvIT 
Fund , in line with our commitment to capital recycling 
and disciplined value unlocking. These assets have an enterprise value of   ~`84,360 Mn , with an expected 
equity realisation of 
 ~`49,000 Mn . This transaction will 
unlock significant value  and free up capital  to pursue 
fresh project addition at Private InvIT.

=== page 21 ===
Given our standard 70:30 debt-to-equity funding model , 
this equity release provides the financial capacity to bid for 
projects worth ~`150,000 Mn .
In essence, by transferring ~`84,360 Mn of stabilised 
assets , we are creating headroom to add ~`150,000 Mn  
of new projects – further reinforcing our focus on capital efficiency, disciplined growth, and long-term value creation .
Strengthening Liquidity through Successful Tap 
Issuance of Overseas Dollar Bonds
Your Company has consistently focused on maintaining a 
robust liquidity position and financial flexibility to support long-term growth and operational stability. In line with this objective, IRB successfully completed a tap issuance of  
US$200 Mn of its 7.11% Senior Secured Notes, originally issued in FY 2023-24 and maturing in FY 2031-32. The issuance was completed at a premium, underscoring investor confidence in IRB’s credit profile, asset quality, and growth outlook.
The proceeds from this issuance were strategically 
utilised for capital expenditure on ongoing projects and for the refinancing of existing debt and enhancing our balance sheet strength. This issuance not only diversifies our funding sources but also improves our overall debt maturity profile.
As the issuer, IRB received international credit ratings of 
‘Ba1’ from Moody’s and ‘BB+’ from Fitch, reflecting the Company’s stable fundamentals and prudent financial management. The Notes are listed on the India International Exchange (IFSC) Limited (India INX), providing enhanced visibility and access to a wider pool of global investors.
This successful transaction further reinforces IRB’s standing 
as a credible issuer in international capital markets and demonstrates our ability to tap global pools of capital efficiently to support infrastructure development in India.
Value Creation for All Stakeholders
At IRB, we are committed to delivering long-term value to all stakeholders  – not only by scaling our business, 
but by ensuring that our partners, investors, and shareholders grow alongside us. This philosophy is rooted in enduring relationships built on trust, performance, and aligned interests .
A notable illustration of this approach was the formation of the Private InvIT in March 2020 , at the peak of the 
COVID-19 crisis. Despite the global uncertainty, GIC affiliates invested with conviction , acquiring a 49% 
stake  in the platform. Their continued participation in 
follow-on opportunities reflects their deep confidence 
in our execution capabilities  and the strength of the 
InvIT framework.
In FY 2024-25, GIC further demonstrated its collaborative, 
long-term approach by accommodating the entry of the Ferrovial Group , facilitating the transfer of a 24% stake in 
the Private InvIT . This transaction enabled GIC to realise 
multi-fold returns  on its original investment in 2020 – a 
clear testament to the  value creation and monetisation 
potential embedded in IRB’s platform .
Another example of our value-driven partnerships is the strategic investment by GIC affiliates and Ferrovial in December 2021 , when both entities committed 
substantial capital to IRB . Their investment provided a 
solid foundation for our next phase of growth, allowing us to pursue larger opportunities with greater financial flexibility . Since then, the value of their investment has 
expanded significantly , reaffirming the resilience of our 
model and the disciplined execution of our strategy.
Crucially, over the last three years, IRB’s stakeholder 
base has expanded tenfold  – a clear reflection of rising 
investor confidence. The number of shareholders grew from 1.55 lakh in December 2021 to 17.62 lakh as of March 2025 . Those who invested in IRB during this 
period have witnessed substantial appreciation in value , 
underscoring the tangible and inclusive nature of the growth we are delivering.
These outcomes reinforce our belief that value creation 
must be broad-based, sustainable, and stakeholder-centric . We remain committed to building on this 
momentum – strengthening our platforms, deepening investor relationships, and delivering consistent returns across economic cycles
.
Other Updates
The Board has declared a total dividend of 30%   
on the face value of equity shares of ` 1 each, taking  
the aggregate dividend payout for FY 2024-25 to  `1,812 Mn , in line with the Company’s stated 
dividend policy.
Our financial fundamentals remain strong . Both India 
Ratings & Research (Ind-Ra)  and CRISIL  have reaffirmed 
IRB’s long-term credit rating at ‘IND AA-’ and ‘AA-’ , 
respectively, with a Stable Outlook  – reflecting continued 
confidence in our robust cash flow visibility, de-risked 
InvIT-led model, and disciplined capital allocation .
As of March 31, 2025 , our t otal order book stands  
at `304,441 Mn , including an EPC order book of  
`23,707 Mn . Factoring in Operations & Maintenance 
(O&M) contracts, our executable pipeline for the next  two years is around ~`50,000 Mn , ensuring healthy 
revenue visibility in the medium term .Beyond Business: Our ESG Initiative
At IRB Infra, our commitment to environmental responsibility 
is deeply rooted in the principles of sustainable development, operational excellence, and proactive leadership . We believe that responsible use of natural 
resources is not just a necessity, but a core driver of long-term value and stakeholder trust.
We have made significant strides in low-carbon 
construction by piloting renewable energy and 
electrification initiatives , such as replacing diesel-heated 
bitumen tanks with electric systems and exploring biomass  
as a cleaner fuel alternative. Our investment in next-generation machinery helps reduce emissions and improve efficiency, while sustainable infrastructure measures – LED 
lighting, solar installations, and eco-friendly materials  – 
are embedded across projects. We also promote a circular economy  by reusing materials like Reclaimed Asphalt 
Product and minimising waste across the value chain.
To preserve biodiversity , especially in ecologically sensitive 
regions, we integrate eco-engineering techniques  into 
design and maintenance – enhancing soil stability, water 
recharge, and natural habitat preservation.
Our CSR programmes  aim to deliver tangible, long-term  
impact across communities through initiatives in healthcare, 
education, environmental conservation , and rural 
development. These efforts are tailored to address local needs and foster inclusive growth.
We uphold a strong culture of governance and 
transparency , supported by a proactive grievance redressal 
system and a Board structure that includes independent directors across all subsidiaries . Our strategic investor, 
Cintra , adds further strength to our governance framework.
IRB is certified for ISO 9001, 14001, 45001, and 27001 – demonstrating our commitment to quality, environment, safety, and information security.
We are proud to have received several accolades, including:
• Skotch ESG Award (Silver) for water conservation at the 
VM7 HAM project
• Best Net Zero Initiative of the Year by UBS Forums
• NSCI Shreshtha Suraksha Puraskar (Silver Trophy and Certificate) for Samarkha Plant at our AVBOT project
• NSCI Certificate of Appreciation for safety performance at our Chittoor–Thachur HAM project
Our Water Positive  status is a milestone we continue to 
uphold, reflecting our commitment to conservation and climate resilience.
At IRB Infra, sustainability is a mindset  – integrated into 
every aspect of our operations. Through innovation, 
accountability, and community-centric initiatives, we remain dedicated to building infrastructure that serves both progress and the planet .
Driving Forward
A significant portion of our value stems from our  asset business , which currently stands at approximately `800 Bn+ . As we move forward, our strategy remains 
focused on building high-quality infrastructure assets , 
even as we continue to monetise mature projects  through 
our platform-based model.
Our EPC business plays a complementary role , supporting 
the development and delivery of our in-house projects 
across both the Private and Public InvITs , covering EPC 
execution and long-term O&M responsibilities . The asset 
business today comprises nearly 85% of our portfolio, underscoring its central role in IRB’s long-term value creation strategy.
Importantly, our Operations & Maintenance (O&M) 
business provides consistent and predictable cash flows , 
with revenue visibility extending over 20 years , driven by 
the long-duration nature of our concession agreements.
Looking ahead, we remain firmly focused on expanding 
our asset base to ` 1.4 trillion  over the next three years – 
reinforcing our position as India’s leading integrated and multi-national infrastructure company.
Gratitude and Commitment
Our vision remains unwavering – to be India’s most admired and trusted infrastructure company , committed 
to building safer, more sustainable, and efficient road networks  that not only connect people but also accelerate 
the nation’s progress.
I extend my heartfelt gratitude to our investors, employees, 
partners, regulatory bodies, and all stakeholders  for their 
continued trust and unwavering support. It is your belief in our vision that fuels our ambition – to dream bigger, execute better, and create lasting impact.
Together, let us continue to pave the way for India’s 
infrastructure future  – with purpose, resilience, 
and excellence.

Our value creation model reflects a deep-rooted commitment to national development, and stakeholder trust. It is futuristic 
and designed to adapt and thrive amidst challenges such as climate change, geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, fluctuating input costs. As we continue to enhance the scale and quality of our operations, we gain greater clarity and confidence in our growth prospects, ensuring long-term value creation.

Stakeholder Engagement and Analysis
In FY 2024-25, our internal respondents representing nine 
stakeholder groups participated in the annual materiality assessment. Survey results were analysed across the dimensions of Stakeholder Concerns, Impact on the Organisation, and Impact on Sustainability, identifying 13 material issues. These issues were reviewed by the ESG Committee.
Integration with Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) 
To enhance the robustness of our assessment, we have fully integrated the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) process. This integration enables us to identify and evaluate risk factors, emerging trends, impact severity, and likelihood of occurrence. It also facilitates the development of ESG strategies and provides deeper insights into sustainability impacts in terms of risks and opportunities.
Additionally, each material topic was evaluated for both 
its positive and negative impacts, including a focused assessment of its implications for human rights. Following GRI 3 guidance, negative impacts were further categorised under three dimensions:
• Caused by the organisation
• Contributed by the organisation
• Directly linkedScoring Methodology
The determination of high-priority material issues was guided by a structured scoring methodology, considering inputs from stakeholder responses and risk assessments. Key dimensions for scoring included:
• Scale: Evaluates the severity of the impact.
• Scope: Assesses the breadth of the impact across affected areas.
• Irremediable Character: Measures the difficulty of reversing or mitigating harm, applicable to negative impacts.
• Likelihood: Considers the probability of occurrence, relevant to potential impacts.
We have also aligned stakeholder expectations with the business risks, enabling us to identify material challenges effectively.  The chart below represents our Materiality Matrix for FY 2024-25, developed through a rigorous double materiality assessment. Each issue is mapped based on its impact on stakeholders (y-axis) and its impact on enterprise value (x-axis).
This matrix illustrates the relative positioning of key Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) topics that were identified as material through survey of internal representatives of stakeholders’, internal risk analysis, and alignment with global reporting frameworks. 
These identified priorities form the backbone of our ESG 
strategy, shaping both our risk management and value creation agenda. The matrix is reviewed annually and updated to reflect evolving stakeholder expectations, business context, and sustainability challenges.

Environmental  
SustainabilityRisk Climate change risks – exacerbated by elevated greenhouse gas emissions – pose multifaceted challenges to infrastructure development and asset management. These risks include increased frequency and severity of extreme weather events, sea-level rise, temperature fluctuations, and changes in precipitation patterns. Such phenomena can accelerate material degradation, disrupt construction timelines, increase maintenance costs, and compromise the long-term structural integrity of critical infrastructure systems.We continue to replace the old vehicles with BS-VI fitted engine vehicles. We are further committed to mitigating the adverse environmental activities. We are committed to the Science Based Target Initiative (SBTi) and are in the process of setting our net zero targets. By complying with ESG guidelines, implementing energy-efficient processes and transitioning to renewable energy sources, we contribute to decarbonisation. We are recycling construction materials to reduce waste generation. We monitor our waste management activities and focuses on reducing waste generation by adopting an effective management system while ensuring compliance CPCB and SPCB guidelines.Negative
Opportunity The adoption of innovative technologies to combat climate change presents valuable opportunities by enhancing operational efficiency and offering a competitive edge. These prospects arise from efforts to expand renewable energy use, minimise water consumption, and develop environmentally beneficial business solutionsPositive

Effective material planning and adhering to waste management guidelines enable the Company to have a minimum negative impact on the environment and business. ABAC Risk Violations of ABAC laws like the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), the U.K. Bribery Act and others can result in fines, sanctions, and even imprisonment. Allegations or findings of bribery or corruption can erode stakeholder trust and damage brand reputation, affecting customer loyalty and investor confidence. Investigations and enforcement actions can disrupt business operations, delay projects, and lead to loss of licenses or contracts. Bribery cases involving third parties such as agents, suppliers, or distributors can expose organisations to indirect liability. Beyond fines, corruption can lead to inflated costs, misallocated resources, and loss of competitive advantage.Complying to ABAC laws mitigate broader enterprise risks, including fraud, conflicts of interest, and unethical behaviour. Preventive vigilance at all level enhances efficiency and accountability which in turn positively impacts productivity and culture of the transparency and fairness. The organisation has developed mandatory e-learning modules on Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML), which are made available to all employees. Strengthening Resilience through Strategic 
Risk Management
Our risk management framework encompasses risks arising from the environmental, social and governance perspective. 
This approach allows us to consider risk events related to climate change, social responsibility and governance practices and develop mitigation strategies for such events.
Risk Governance
The Board constituted a Risk Management Committee that oversees the implementation of the risk management policy, including evaluating the adequacy of risk management systems.
The Committee is updated semi-annually on the potential 
risks, including climate-related risks and relevant mitigation measures for the same. The Committee also provides guidance for enhancing the Company’s resilience.We understand the importance of addressing risks proactively to safeguard our 
stakeholder’s interests and ensure long-term sustainability.  To achieve this, we have established a robust risk management mechanism that systematically identifies, assesses, monitors and mitigates risks that could potentially impact our operations. We believe that by taking a proactive approach to risk management, we can effectively mitigate potential threats and capitalise on opportunities that align with our strategic objectives.
The Company has in place dedicated teams at the 
Function-level and Site-level to ensure that the relevant mitigation measures are implemented in real time and at all levels. Moreover, periodic business function & project reviews are conducted to ensure that timely actions are taken for identified risks. These also include discussions on risks specific to each function or project, including climate-related risks.All risks and risk events with a significant risk intensity and their control measures are reported to the Risk Management Committee on a Quarterly basis. The Risk Management Committee is briefed on the status of mitigation measures regularly and if significant breakdowns in risk controls are observed, the Committee instructs risk owners for corrective action.
Risk Culture and Training
IRB’s risk culture is based on the principles of openness, 
transparency, accountability, ethics, empowering risk owners to take informed decisions and continual improvement. This is achieved by setting the tone at the top, imparting comprehensive training, conducting awareness sessions across corporate functions.
The leadership ensures that business objectives, policies 
and the importance of risk management are clearly articulated throughout the organisation.
The risk management training encompasses understanding 
the Company’s risk management policy, creation of risk registers, risk assessment and evaluation, mitigation measures and understanding of best practices of risk management as per globally renowned risk management frameworks.The risk management process at IRB enhances the organisation’s ability to prevent or mitigate potential negative impacts after due consideration of any associated potential opportunity. It allows for proactive decision-making, resource allocation and the establishment of robust control mechanisms. The Company fosters a strong culture to take informed decisions while carefully evaluating the impact of risks in protecting its assets, reputation and overall objectives.
Each department is responsible for identifying and 
managing risks specific to their area of expertise. The Company has also deployed dedicated teams responsible for assessing and mitigating risks associated with each project. Regular risk assessments and proactive risk mitigation strategies are integrated into bidding, project planning and execution.
This approach encourages employees to not only 
identify and report risks but also to take ownership of these risks, creating a culture of shared responsibility and accountability. This practice helps the Company in developing a robust risk management culture.

Risk Management Process
Risk events are systematically identified, assessed and 
prioritised based on their likelihood of occurrence and potential impact on established objectives. Following the identification of risks, a thorough description is provided and identified risks are assessed based on the Risk Evaluation Framework to estimate their potential impact and likelihood of occurrence. Specific control measures are evaluated to mitigate each of the risks. The combination of the potential impact of a risk and its likelihood is used to determine its intensity and scores are calculated to carry out analysis. Using this process and in alignment with SEBI LODR, IRB’s ERM framework addresses risks under 5 categories of risks.
Some of the key risks under these categories are given below:
For detailed analysis of these risks, please refer to page 135-136 under management discussion section of statutory

Emerging Risks
In our ongoing commitment to comprehensive risk 
management, IRB acknowledges the need of identifying emerging risks which are crucial for safeguarding our long-term objectives. We keep track of global emerging risks highlighted by World Economic Forum & Gartner Global emerging risk report. It is our constant endeavour to understand and incorporate them in our risk universe, wherever found applicable.
These risks are further classified into strategic, compliance 
and governance-related, financial, IT-related and operational categories. By systematically identifying and addressing these emerging risks, we enhance our ability to mitigate potential threats and capitalise on opportunities, ensuring that our risk management approach remains robust and aligned with our strategic goals. This proactive identification and categorisation process, integrated into our multi-level risk reporting and regular assessments, enables us to navigate uncertainties effectively while reinforcing our commitment to resilience and long-term success.One of the key emerging risks identified is being managed 
as described below:
IT and CybersecurityAs a responsible organisation, we understand the 
significance of information technology and cybersecurity in our daily operations. It is our responsibility to safeguard vital information in the cyber world to ensure the security of our business. As we continue to digitise and automate, we recognise the importance of using cyber tools and utilities to fuel our growth and expansion.
With the increase in frequency of cyberattacks on vital 
digital infrastructure occurring globally, our IT function has proactively implemented substantial measures to safeguard the organisation against potential threats. Critical information is protected from unauthorised access, use, disclosure, modification, and disposal, whether intentional or unintentional. To safeguard the integrity of data and guarantee its uninterrupted and on demand availability to the users, suitable measures are in place for recovery of data. Thus, in the event of any manmade or natural disaster, cyberattack, malfunctioning or failure of hardware at central location, our IT Team remains available with least amount 
of downtime or data loss. Additionally, we implement Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) from third party to proactively identify and address potential cybersecurity risks, fortifying our highway construction and maintenance systems against cyber-attacks, data manipulation, and service disruptions.
Climate-related Risks and Opportunities
At IRB, we have integrated climate-related risks in our business strategy, operations and financial decision-making processes. This includes identification of climate-related risks and opportunities to understand the impact of these 
   Governance
The governance pillar 
addresses IRB’s approach to managing climate-related risks and opportunities. This encompasses the structures and processes in place to ensure effective oversight, management, and integration of climate considerations into decision-making at the highest levels. Risk Management
The risk management pillar focuses on the mechanisms that we are employing to identify, assess, monitor and mitigate climate-related risks. This involves a comprehensive examination of the tools and processes in place to manage the evolving landscape of climate-related risks.   Strategy
The strategy pillar explores the potential impacts of climate-related risks and opportunities on our operations, strategy and financial planning. It delves into how climate considerations are factored into IRB’s overarching strategy and long-term planning. Metrics and Targets
The metrics and targets pillar involves the disclosure of our commitment regarding the assessment and management of relevant climate-related risks and opportunities. Governance
At IRB, climate-related governance is integrated at the 
highest levels of decision-making. The Board-level Risk Management Committee (RMC) holds strategic oversight on environmental and climate-related risks and opportunities. The Committee routinely assesses IRB’s exposure to climate impacts, evolving regulatory landscapes, and progress against sustainability targets.
As part of IRB’s enterprise-wide risk review and business 
continuity planning, climate change considerations are formally embedded. Projects with potential vulnerability to climate risks undergo rigorous assessment and engineering interventions in accordance with relevant Authority’s procedures & guidelines. This includes climate-resilient project design and its execution under the supervision of an Independent Engineer appointed by Authority and Authority’s officials. The executed projects are operationalised after obtaining necessary clearances from Authority, ensuring robust internal controls.This governance approach enables IRB to proactively address climate-related risks while capitalising on low-carbon transition opportunities, particularly in areas such as energy efficiency, and sustainable infrastructure development.
Strategy
IRB has defined its short-term (0–5 years), medium-term (5–10 years), and long-term (Beyond 10 years) strategy after a comprehensive peer benchmarking exercise. These time frames form the basis for assessing the materiality of climate-related risks and opportunities and are embedded into risk reviews, strategic planning, and investment decision frameworks.
Based on the IPCC RCP Scenarios and seven NGFS climate 
scenarios, IRB has proactively identified a spectrum of transition risks, physical risks, and emerging opportunities across its diversified portfolio of businesses – ranging from BOT and TOT to HAM and airport operations. These insights help shape IRB’s medium- and long-term resilience strategy under the framework of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).
For identifying and assessing physical risks, IRB has 
considered IPCC’s Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP), RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5. For transition risks, IRB utilised India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Below 2°C Scenario, NGFS Current Policy and Net Zero 2050 Scenarios.
We mapped the plausible business impact of the following 
categories of risks and opportunities:Physical Risks
Physical risks are a result of short-term catastrophes (acute) 
or long-term variations in climate patterns (chronic). Acute physical risks are those that are triggered by a specific event, such as extreme weather events like cyclones, storms or floods. Whereas longer-term changes in climatic patterns (e.g. prolonged higher temperatures) may produce sea level rise or chronic heat waves, which are referred to as chronic physical hazards.
Transition Risks
Transition risks are enterprise risks that arise as a result 
of societal and economic transformations toward a low-carbon, more environmentally friendly future. These risks can include policy and regulatory and legal risks, technological risks, market risks and reputational risks. These areas can vary in terms of their type, focus and geographical acceptance, which can have a financial implication on our business.

KEY METRICS TRACKED INCLUDE:

Agra Etawah NH19Risk Management
IRB integrates climate-related risks into its Enterprise Risk 
Management (ERM) framework using a structured, scenario-based approach. Climate risks are identified and assessed across physical and transition categories, drawing on inputs from site-level qualitative assessments under IPCC RCPs and NGFS pathways, and stakeholder consultations. The risks are evaluated for materiality based on their likelihood, business unit vulnerability, and potential financial impact, and are prioritised using a composite scoring model. 
These climate risks are reviewed periodically by 
the Risk Management Committee and incorporated into the corporate risk register alongside traditional operational, financial, and regulatory risks. Mitigation measures – ranging from capital expenditure decisions to adaptation strategies – are integrated into business planning cycles. This process ensures that climate risk is not treated as a standalone issue but is embedded into the Company’s governance, planning, and performance evaluation mechanisms.
This framework is tailored to consider objectives pertaining 
to operations, reporting, and compliance. Leveraging this, IRB systematically evaluates risks and opportunities at both the asset/plant and corporate levels. The mitigation plans and advancements toward achieving low-carbon and sustainable development targets undergo thorough review and approval by the ESG Committee and RMC and inform business continuity planning, site-level investments, and the Company’s broader climate strategy. This integrated approach ensures climate risk is managed alongside conventional operational, regulatory, and financial risks, as part of a unified Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework.

Waste Management
We actively work to reduce waste generation across our project sites and offices by deploying robust waste management systems. Our practices adhere to the regulatory guidelines set by the Central and State Pollution Control Boards (CPCB and SPCB), and are guided by the principles of reduce, reuse, and recycle. This ensures that we not only comply with statutory requirements but also significantly decrease the volume of waste sent to landfills, promoting a circular economy mindset.
Energy Efficiency and Decarbonisation
Energy conservation is a key pillar of our environmental strategy. We continuously adopt energy-efficient technologies and operational practices that lower consumption while improving performance. A significant part of this journey involves transitioning to renewable energy sources – an effort aligned with our broader decarbonisation roadmap and global climate commitments.Water Stewardship
Water is a critical resource, especially in infrastructure development, and we are committed to its efficient and responsible use. Our water management practices include the use of water-saving technologies, recycling wastewater through STPs and sedimentation tanks, applying drip irrigation, and replacing conventional curing methods with water-efficient alternatives. In alignment with government initiatives such as the Sujalam Sufalam Jal Abhiyan, we contribute to community-based water conservation projects that not only replenish local water bodies but also benefit thousands of people in nearby villages.
Climate Action
Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions is integral to our sustainability agenda. We are progressively implementing ESG-aligned practices, improving operational efficiency, and scaling up the use of clean energy sources. These steps support our transition toward low-carbon infrastructure and reinforce our contribution to national and global climate goals.
Through these integrated efforts, we aim not only to comply 
with environmental regulations but also to lead by example in promoting sustainable infrastructure development.

Performance Review
FY 2024-25 marked a phase of stable profitability and 
disciplined execution for IRB, supported by resilient cash flows, sustained margins, and incremental benefits from maturing toll concessions across its Private and Public InvIT portfolios. 
EBITDA declined slightly to ` 40,239 Mn, though the margin 
held steady at 50%, reflecting strong cost optimisation and 
operational discipline. Profit Before Tax (PBT) increased to `10,573  Mn from ` 9,514 Mn in FY 2023-24, while Profit 
After Tax (PAT) increased ` 6,766 Mn* – driven by effective 
tax management and stronger internal accruals. This translated into a Net Profit Margin of ~9% before exceptional 
items (net), despite continued investments in new project acquisitions and capital deployment. Our resilient performance reaffirms IRB’s ability to preserve profitability in a dynamic cost environment through a balanced mix of annuity and toll-based revenue streams.
The Debtors Turnover Ratio improved to 5.35 times in 
FY 2024-25, up from 4.02 in FY 2023-24 and a low of 2.86 in FY 2022-23. This sharp improvement reflects enhanced billing efficiency, faster collections, and better receivables management across EPC and O&M contracts.Conversely, the Net Debt to Equity ratio declined to 0.59x 
in FY 2024-25, compared to 0.87x in FY 2023-24. This was driven by higher short-term liabilities linked to project mobilisation, toll operations, and vendor payments. While the ratio remains within infrastructure sector norms, prudent working capital planning will remain a priority to maintain liquidity headroom.
In a year characterised by both scale and complexity, this 
sustained profitability performance reflects the strength of our business model – built on predictable cash flows from long-tenure concessions, disciplined financial management, and an agile project execution approach.
Earnings Per Share (EPS) remained consistent at ` 1.12 for 
FY 2024-25 (before exceptional items - net)  signifying 
steady shareholder earnings amid business expansion. The near-term earnings will remain supported by strong internal accruals, while longer-term gains will be unlocked through the completion of large-scale assets and timely monetisation through the InvIT platform.Financial Capital

In-House Execution and O&M Excellence
IRB’s fully integrated in-house capabilities – spanning 
Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) as well as Operations and Maintenance (O&M) – enable seamless execution across the entire lifecycle of its infrastructure assets. 
As of FY 2024-25, our EPC division is backed by a robust 
order book of `24 Bn, reflecting a strong pipeline of 
projects under implementation. Complementing this is our O&M portfolio, which has scaled significantly to cover contracts worth ` 281 Bn, underscoring the trust placed 
in us for long-term asset stewardship. Our execution strength is driven by a dedicated workforce of over 3,090 construction personnel, supported by a `5 Bn fleet of high-performance construction equipment. To ensure 
operational continuity and resource efficiency, IRB operates 
leased quarries and hot-mix plants at strategic locations, enabling assured raw material supply and quality control. 
We have also made strides in sustainable operations by 
deploying solar-powered installations at select project sites,  including our Hyderabad facility (NORR) and along the Agra-Etawah Tollway. Projects. Additionally, VK1 project has been equipped with dedicated solar backup system, further strengthening our renewable energy integration at the project level. The integration of centralised digital project monitoring systems with automated tolling infrastructure further enhances our capability to maximise asset uptime, reduce operational costs, and deliver a superior commuter experience. This digital backbone enables real-time 
decision-making and predictive maintenance, reinforcing our position as a technology leader in the highway infrastructure sector.
Embedding Excellence Through Certified 
Management Systems
As a part of our commitment to operational excellence 
and asset integrity, we have embedded globally recognised management systems across our infrastructure assets. Our major project sites, toll plazas, and operational hubs are certified under ISO 9001 (Quality Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety Management). These integrated systems form a foundational layer of our manufactured capital, ensuring consistent quality, regulatory compliance, and safety across our operations. The implementation of these standards strengthens our ability to deliver reliable, safe, and sustainable transport infrastructure.
Asset Performance and Utilisation
We maintain rigorous performance tracking mechanisms 
to ensure seamless toll operations and high asset availability across our network. 
Our systems are built to deliver reliability and speed 
at scale:
• Asset uptime consistently exceeds 98%, minimising operational disruptions and maximising revenue potential
• We manage an average daily traffic (ADT) of 1.3 Mn vehicles, underscoring the critical role of our corridors in national connectivity
• Our tolling infrastructure is equipped with real-time data capture and automated reconciliation systems, allowing for transparent, efficient processing of toll transactions
Accelerating Infrastructure through Digital 
Integration
Our tolling infrastructure has undergone a significant 
digital transformation – notably through FASTag, the government-mandated electronic toll collection system, and the deployment of advanced toll management solutions at all toll plazas. These systems work in tandem to ensure seamless, contactless toll transactions that reduce delays, minimise human intervention, and enhance operational control. Our toll plazas have achieved FASTag penetration rates exceeding 97%, aligning with the national average and significantly 
reducing congestion, vehicle idling time, emissions, and cash handling risks. Deployment of the latest toll management systems with integration of RFID technology further streamlines vehicle throughput by enabling real-time identification, authentication, and lane access. These systems ensure accurate, tamper-proof revenue collections while reducing human intervention. The use of intelligent platforms not only enhances financial control but also provides a smoother travel experience for commuters.
This digital transformation is not merely a regulatory 
compliance measure – it is a cornerstone of operational efficiency. Offerings include real-time traffic and revenue monitoring, reduced average transaction time per vehicle, improved asset utilisation and toll lane throughput, and enhanced commuter experience and transparency.
In tandem with our robust physical infrastructure, this high 
level of digital enablement underscores our commitment to smart, future-ready transport systems. It also reflects our alignment with national priorities such as Gati Shakti, Bharatmala, and the National Logistics Policy. 
With continued investments in both physical and digital 
infrastructure, we are well-positioned to deliver long-term value to stakeholders while supporting India’s journey toward seamless, connected, and sustainable mobility.

Employee Engagement

Management Philosophy
At IRB Group, the safety of our workforce is our foremost 
priority across all offices and project sites. Our commitment to health and safety is reflected in our KPI target ‘to strive for incident-free operations and foster a generational shift in EHS culture’. It underscores our dedication to fostering a safer work environment for employees, contractors, and value chain partners. This commitment is realised through the implementation of rigorous systems and procedures.
We ensure that our health and safety processes are 
continuously monitored, audited, and reviewed to identify trends, implement control measures, and assess compliance, which are integral to our operations. Our goal is to cultivate an incident-free, environmentally sustainable, and socially responsible organisation by adhering to the highest safety standards, including the NHAI Safety Manual, MoRTH, applicable IRC guidelines, as well as industry best practices.
Regular management review meetings and Board-level 
assessments provide us with opportunities to evaluate the effectiveness of our safety measures and pinpoint areas for improvement. This dedication to continuous enhancement is vital for maintaining high health and safety standards within our organisation.
The Corporate Health, Safety, and Welfare (HSW) Policy 
is implemented through a comprehensive framework that includes procedures, guidelines, and manuals. Safety is integrated at all levels of the organisation, with each employee playing a crucial and responsible role. Dedicated Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS) representatives and teams at every business and project site collaborate closely with proactive and skilled site teams to enforce the Company’s safety practices and implement specific EHS interventions tailored to relevant risks.
EHS training is essential both prior to project 
commencement and on an ongoing basis, serving as a key component of our safety measures. The Company’s safety 
performance is reviewed monthly during management meetings and quarterly at the Board level to ensure continuous improvement.Human Capital

We prioritise the health and safety of all employees & 
workers on our sites. Sub-contractors are assessed for their safety capabilities as outlined in agreements before contracts are awarded, and they are required to comply with our policies. IRB ensures its commitment through regular training, site visits, and both internal and external audits.
Safety committees are established at each project 
site, comprising representatives from senior management, project teams, and subcontractors. These committees convene regularly with a structured agenda, emphasising compliance and the implementation of necessary safety measures. They serve as a critical mechanism for driving the Company’s safety objectives in alignment with its overall vision and strategic goals.
To foster a robust safety culture, it is crucial to 
continuously highlight safety hazards and risks, engaging everyone in our safety initiatives. Our goal is to keep safety at the forefront of everyone’s mind, ensuring that all employees return home safely every day.Building a Health & Safety Culture by:
RISK REDUCTION 
 
It helps to identify and mitigate potential hazards, reducing the likelihood of accidents and injuries in the workplace.
PROACTIVE RISK MANAGEMENT 
 
HIRA allows organisations to identify potential hazards before they lead to incidents, enabling proactive measures to mitigate risks.
ENHANCED SAFETY 
 
By systematically assessing risks, HIRA helps create safer work environments, reducing the likelihood of accidents and injuries.
INFORMED DECISION-MAKING  
 
HIRA provides valuable data that informs safety policies, procedures, and resource allocation, ensuring that safety measures are targeted and effective.
EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT  
 
Involving employees in the HIRA process fosters a culture of safety, encouraging them to take ownership of their safety and that of their colleagues.
CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT 
 
HIRA is an ongoing process that promotes continuous monitoring and improvement of safety practices, adapting to new risks as they arise.EMPLOYEE WELL-BEING 
 
Prioritising safety fosters a healthier work environment, enhancing employee morale and overall well-being.
REGULATORY COMPLIANCE 
 
Implementing significant safety initiatives ensures adherence to legal and regulatory standards, minimising the risk of fines and legal issues.
COST SAVINGS 
 
By preventing accidents and injuries, organisations  can save costs on medical, insurance, and potential litigation expenses.
REPUTATION ENHANCEMENT 
 
A strong commitment to safety enhances an organisation’s reputation, attracting talent and building trust with clients and stakeholders.
CULTURAL SHIFT 
 
It promotes a culture of safety, encouraging employees to prioritise safety in their daily activities and decision-making.
We conduct various internal and external safety audits, including client audits and Integrated Management System (IMS) audits, at our sites and offices. These audits are carried out in accordance with the requirements & fulfilment of ISO 45001 for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems.
We place special emphasis on the design and 
implementation of Safety Management Plans (SMP), Traffic Management Plans (TMP), in alignment with client requirements, particularly at project sites.
Safety performance is reviewed during Board meetings, 
where direction and guidance are provided. An EHS Steering Committee is established for every business unit, and a Safety Committee is in place for each project site, both of which effectively monitor safety performance.Notable Safety Endeavours/Significant Safety Initiatives

EHS Induction Room 
We have established an EHS Induction room at all our construction projects. This designated space educates workers and employees about EHS protocols. It serves as a platform for communicating EHS systems, guidelines, emergency procedures, and incident reporting processes, as well as ensuring regulatory and legal compliance. This initiative promotes a culture of safety on the construction site by informing workers about their roles and responsibilities related to health and safety, including the importance of reporting. incidents and near misses.
SAFETY PRECAUTIONS  WHILE  WORKING WITH  WINCH TRIPOD  IN PILING ACTIVITY
➢Cranes (Company owned or hired) to be 
thoroughly inspected by competent person. TPI 
certificate to be obtained for Equipment,   tools & 
tackles which are in-use
➢Always secure lifted load  by using  appropriate D-
shackles,  wire rope, web slings, chain  link etc. 
➢Compaction  of ground surface shall be ensured 
before marching the crane & tripod erection.
➢Maintain clear communication channels by 
deploying trained/experienced signalman  between 
workers, supervisors, crane operator and helper.
➢Report any safety concerns or near misses  
promptly to supervisors / engineers.
➢Continuous, responsible and vigilant supervision 
by trained and experienced personnel is must  
during the activity. 
➢Guide ropes shall be used  with  safe distance 
between workers and the crane during the activity.
➢Do not allow, use of mobile  phones/headphones 
while working.
➢Take extra precautions during rainy  season and 
other  adverse weather conditions. 
➢Emergency contact details shall be communicated  
before starting the activity.
➢Ensure that bore  holes are covered with  hard 
covers / strong rebar mesh to avoid fall of person.
➢Use appropriate PPE’s  during  activity such as high -
visibility jackets, safety shoes, safety helmets etc.
➢Ensure Tool-Box Talk (TBT) / Safety briefing is 
imparted before start of work activities .At Construction sites, typically tripods are 
used for winch and other  piling operations. In 
the past, incidents had occurred due to the 
collapse  of Tripod for the following reasons : 
▪Unsafe access to workplace.
▪Lapses in lifting & shifting operations.
▪Lack  of Hazard Identification and inadequate 
control measures.
▪Use of Damaged Lifting  Tools & tackles such as 
D-shackle, wire rope web sling  , chain  link etc.
▪Engaging Uncertified Vehicle or Equipment.
▪Uneven &/or Wet ground Surface.
▪Miscommunication  between Operator & 
Workers.
▪Signalman or Bankman not provided.
▪SOP or Methodology not followed.
▪Environmental Factors: Adverse weather 
conditions such as high  winds, heavy rain,  fog. 
Natural Calamities  like earthquake, landslide, 
cyclone, flood  etc.
▪Engaging untrained workforce including  
operator.
▪Bored pile hole not covered after piling  
operation.
Following Safety Precautions Need 
to be Taken to Prevent Incidents:
➢Methodology & Risk  Assessment  specific  to the 
activity shall be followed in right spirit.
➢Provide EHS  induction training along with  job-
specific training to all concerned.

stakeholder groups such as toll users, local communities, schools, healthcare facilities, and the environment.CSR Governance
The  Company has constituted a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee in compliance with Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013. The Committee primarily oversees the execution of the Company’s CSR policy and timely progress of the programmes. As of March 31, 2025, the Committee is composed of 4 members, including 1 independent director.
The CSR Committee of the Company functions under the oversight of the Board of Directors. The Committee is responsible 
for formulation, implementation and periodically reviewing the CSR policy to fulfil the Company’s social and environmental objectives. It also seeks to guide the Board in the formulation of CSR action plans and amount of funds to be allocated to the respective programmes. Further, the overall implementation and monitoring of the programme remain under the purview of the CSR committee. 
The overall vision of the Committee is to integrate social and environmental objectives with the overall business strategy of 
the Company. In addition to this, the CSR committee reviews the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) of the Company.

Social & Relationship Capital - Responsible Sourcing
Fostering Meaningful 
Supplier Relationships
As a purpose-driven organisation, we recognise that responsible sourcing is more than a 
mere business practice; it is ingrained in our core values and guiding principles. We are committed to a sustainable future and our approach to sourcing reflects this unwavering dedication. Traceability and transparency are paramount in our responsible sourcing initiatives, ensuring we meet both environmental needs and stakeholder expectations.The construction industry’s intricate supply chains, 
spanning numerous tiers and diverse materials, present a complex challenge for responsible sourcing. We are committed to working with our suppliers by ensuring that materials are sourced ethically and sustainably, with consideration for labour rights, environmental impact and community well-being, which has necessitated proper due diligence and robust supplier management practices.
A well-established network of responsible suppliers allowed 
us to both mitigate the risks inherent in our supply chain and identify the opportunities for a greener economy.
We follow our standard operating procedure for requisition 
and procurement, applicable to all sites, workers and employees of our suppliers. This includes temporary, permanent and contract workers, as well as subcontractors. 
Additionally, the Company, by utilising Crumb Rubber 
Modified Bitumen (CRMB 55 – 2,923 tonnes; CRMB 60 – 26,564 tonnes consumed in FY 2024-25), contributes to the global efforts to tackle the waste tyre issue. CRMB is a blend of bitumen and crumb rubber derived from waste tyres, helping to repurpose millions of tyres that would otherwise occupy landfills for centuries. Additionally, we sourced 79 MT of curing compound under our sustainable sourcing initiatives during the reporting period.
These responsible sourcing practices contribute to reducing 
greenhouse gas emissions, conserving natural resources, We believe in fostering an ethical and sustainable supply 
chain that respects human rights, ensures fair labour practices and prioritises environmental stewardship.
We are committed to building roads and highways while 
prioritising environmental sustainability and responsible sourcing practices. Our approach focuses on utilising innovative materials and techniques that reduce environmental impact, conserve resources and enhance the durability and performance of infrastructure.
We continue to scale the use of recycled and low-impact 
alternatives to traditional materials. The table below highlights the Y-o-Y replacement share for key inputs such as pond ash, M-sand, iron slag, and GGBS, reflecting our commitment to resource efficiency and circular construction practices.
